rules.rationale: Halides showed the most negative source refractive-index effect; low anion polarizability inverts to wide band gaps.
Chalcogenides raised source index; polarizable S/Se/Te p-states lift the valence band and shrink gaps.
Largest positive source effect; covalent metalloid networks are canonical narrow-gap semiconductors under Moss inversion.
High mean-Z boosted source index; diffuse heavy orbitals widen bands and reduce measured gaps.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers source dielectric effects with reversed sign via the Moss inverse index-gap relation. Fails where high index and wide gap coexist, such as heavy ionic oxides, or when low source confidence makes inversion unreliable.

rules.rationale: Main-group halides are maximally ionic; closed-shell cations add no d-states, giving the widest experimental gaps.
Large electronegativity difference and deep O 2p valence band place oxides high on the ionicity ladder.
Chalcogen-dominated compositions form weakly ionic covalent semiconductors with small experimental gaps.
Counter-hypothesis: reverses the near-zero-confidence source lanthanide relation; partly filled f-states add in-gap levels.

skills.hypothesis: Ranks by cation-anion electronegativity difference and reverses the lowest-confidence source relation on lanthanides. Fails for d0 transition-metal oxides and defect-dominated experimental samples whose measured gaps depart from ionicity ordering.

lesson: Across two independent eight-seed development batches the Moss-inverted transfer skill led on mean AUC (72.7 then 74.9) while the ionicity ladder trailed (65.3 then 72.6), and each skill collapsed on different single seeds, so instability is seed-specific rather than skill-specific. Two separate batches favoring the same skill is weaker evidence than a controlled study but stronger than one batch, so the source-grounded inversion is frozen and the ionicity ladder is retained as the mechanistic counter-hypothesis.
revision_summary: Fixed the schema failure: every conditions entry is now a JSON object mapping a real catalog field directly to one exact catalog value, with the single two-key interaction limited to the chemically meaningful main-group halide case. Skill IDs are short snake_case, each skill has four rules, rationales under 25 words, hypotheses under 45 words, and all parameters inside allowed ranges. The source-grounded Moss inversion keeps its best-performing rule set (halide, chalcogenide, metalloid, mean_z_high) and is selected; the domain skill swaps the pnictide and transition-metal terms for a chalcogen-dominant penalty and an explicit lanthanide counter-hypothesis that reverses the lowest-confidence source relation. Source transfer evidence is unchanged and no target outcomes or candidate identifiers are referenced.
